In the opinion of many non-Marxist and some Marxist scholars, this was the crucial initial step in the elaboration of a deviationist doctrine which not only departed from Marx's and Engels' original thought, but which eventually overshadowed it. Plekhanov, in this view, served as the link between Engels and Lenin in which a tendency in Engels toward a mechanistic materialism, manifested in his Anti-Dühring and The Dialectics of Nature, was developed into a dominant theme.

results.title: Justin Steinberg, Russian Marxism and the Materialist Interpretation of Spinoza
results.snippet: Nevertheless, Spinoza has often been read as a materialist, and one prominent strand of this materialist reading may be traced back to the Russian Marxist Georgi Plekhanov, who, beginning in the 1890s, engaged in a series of polemics in which he defended a comprehensive materialist reading of Spinoza—one that would cover both ontological and dialectical materialism, or “old” and “new” materialism—that would cement Spinoza’s status as the great progenitor of political radicalism.

Spinoza is not a materialist, at least not as typically understood today. He is a substance monist and a pluralist about what kinds of things exist. Nevertheless, Spinoza has often been ...

In this paper, I analyze the distinct materialist readings of Spinoza advanced by Deborin, Akselrod, and Plekhanov. I argue that Deborin’s approach, according to which Spinoza identifies Being with matter, fails as an interpretation, that Akselrod’s alternative, according to which ideas are in some sense asymmetrically dependent on bodies, fails either as an interpretation of Spinoza or as an account of materialism, leaving Plekhanov’s interpretation of Spinoza, which takes materialism to be compatible with panpsychism, as the most plausible of the bunch.
